data.title: Solidly-stable / Camelot / Aerodrome stable calc port
data.body:
## Goal
- Port the solidly-stable invariant (Camelot stable + Aerodrome V2 stable) out of pure Python — disposition between a new Rust leaf or folding onto an existing CL/constant-product core.

## Context
- Python: `src/degenbot/calculations/camelot.py`, `src/degenbot/calculations/solidly_stable.py`, `src/degenbot/aerodrome/v2_pool_calc.py`, `src/degenbot/uniswap/v2_pool_calc.py` (Camelot stable branch folded in by slice 7 step 4a).
- Design memo ergo `WFY235` chose strategy-on-`LiquidityPool` companion (Option A/D) over a separate Rust variant. Camelot/Aerodrome stable calc currently stays Python (ADR-005 B-ii); this task re-evaluates now that `degenbot-curve-math`/`-balancer-math` leaves exist.
- Known pre-existing bug: `calc_exact_in_stable` arity mismatch (TODO-7ea2e7d9) — resolve as part of the evaluation.

## Acceptance
- Disposition recorded (`port-now` vs `stays-python` with criterion). If `port-now`: pure-Rust leaf lands under §3.A, wrapped + routed, parity cross-checked against the Python oracle; `_state_cache` Aerodrome-specific tests rewritten if construction sites change.
- TODO-7ea2e7d9 resolved or re-triaged.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`; `just test-rust-python`; `just test-python`; `just lint-rust`; `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`; `just lint-python`; `just format`

> Rubric §2 evaluation — disposition: `done`. The Solidly-stable / Camelot
> invariant math + the Aerodrome companion swap-calc orchestration now
> route through the pure-Rust `degenbot-solidly-math` leaf. Sub-steps
> A + B + B' (umbrella re-export) + C (companion routing) + D (parity
> cross-check) all landed in commit 5dd4da68.

## Disposition record + cutover log

### Sub-step A — pure-Rust core leaf (`degenbot-solidly-math`)
**New crate** `rust/crates/degenbot-solidly-math/` (ADR-005 slice 12f).
Mirrors `degenbot-curve-math` (slice 11c) + `degenbot-balancer-math`
(slice 12e) shape: standalone, `pyo3`-free, `tokio`-free crate depending
only on `alloy::primitives`.

- `src/lib.rs`: crate root + the `ONE` (10^18) constant + the
  `SolidlyMathError` enum (`Overflow` / `InvalidTokenIn` / `DidNotConverge`
  — plain `#[derive]` enum, no `thiserror` dep, mirrors the
  `BalancerMathError` shape with the binding layer handling PyErr
  conversion directly).
- `src/solidly.rs`: `calc_d`, `calc_k`, `calc_f`, `calc_exact_in_volatile`,
  `get_y_solidly`, `calc_exact_in_stable_solidly` (Solidly / Aerodrome).
- `src/camelot.rs`: `f_camelot`, `k_camelot`, `get_y_camelot`,
  `calc_exact_in_stable_camelot` (Camelot variant — same invariant shape
  but the deployed-Camelot contract's operation-ordering & simpler
  convergence check).

**Design choices:**
- The Python oracle's closure-injected `calc_exact_in_stable(k_func,
  get_y_func)` becomes two **pre-baked entrypoints** — one per
  `(k_func, get_y_func)` pair the companions actually use
  (`calc_exact_in_stable_solidly` uses `calc_k` + `get_y_solidly`;
  `calc_exact_in_stable_camelot` uses `k_camelot` + `get_y_camelot`).
  Avoids `dyn Fn` indirection in the hot path.
- Python's `fee: Fraction` argument becomes two `U256`s (`fee_numer` +
  `fee_denom`) at the seam — keeps the pure-math leaf `num-rational`-free
  (the alloy-only constraint the leaf maintains).
- Solidity-arithmetic overflow + non-convergence checked via
  `checked_mul` on `calc_k`'s `a*b` (matches the Python oracle's
  `raise_if_invalid_uint256(a*b)` revert — `wrapping_mul` would silently
  modulo-wrap past `MAX_UINT256` and miss the revert; `checked_mul`
  bubbles `Overflow`).
- `f_camelot`: the deployed-Camelot operation-ordering (different
  intermediate-rounding from Solidly) is preserved via explicit
  `yy` / `yyy` / `xxx` temporaries (the Python source is left-
  associative-with-`*`/`//` chains; naively transliterating to a single
  Rust expression with `.wrapping_mul(ONE).wrapping_mul(y)` mis-parses
  the `.method()` binding tighter than `/` and produces wrong rounding).

### Sub-step B — PyO3 wrapper (`degenbot-python/src/solidly_math/`)
- `lib.rs`: 10 `#[pyfunction]`s wrapping every ported entrypoint (the
  full step-function set: `solidly_calc_d`, `solidly_calc_k`,
  `solidly_calc_f`, `camelot_f`, `camelot_k`; the iterative solvers
  `solidly_get_y_solidly`, `camelot_get_y_camelot`; the pre-baked
  orchestration entrypoints `solidly_calc_exact_in_volatile`,
  `solidly_calc_exact_in_stable_solidly`,
  `solidly_calc_exact_in_stable_camelot`). Mirrors the `balancer_math` /
  `curve_math` binding-layer shape: `extract_u256` / `u256_to_py_obj`
  round-trip helpers + a `solidly_err` error translator.
- `mod.rs`: module-tree re-export.
- Cargo feature `solidly-math` (default-on) in `degenbot-python/Cargo.toml`
  gating the optional path-dep; registered in `c_api.rs::register()` and
  declared in the `degenbot_rs.pyi` stub (10 `def`s with full signatures
  so `ty` can statically check the Python callsites that route through
  the seam).

### Sub-step B' — umbrella re-export + standalone-consumer smoke
- `rust/crates/degenbot/src/lib.rs`: `pub use degenbot_solidly_math;`
  (alongside the existing `degenbot_curve_math` / `degenbot_balancer_math`
  re-exports — the ADR-005 standalone-Rust-consumer surface).
- `rust/crates/degenbot/Cargo.toml`: pulls `degenbot-solidly-math` as a
  pyo3-free path-dep.
- `rust/crates/degenbot/examples/standalone_consumer.rs`: extended (step
  6) with a Solidly `calc_d(x0, y)` + `calc_f(x0, y)` direct-port identity
  check (re-derived in plain integer arithmetic and asserted equal to the
  Rust leaf's result — no `pyo3` import in the build graph).
- `rust/Cargo.toml`: workspace member + `[profile.release.package.
  degenbot-solidly-math] codegen-units = 16` (consistency with the other
  pure-Rust cores — the cdylib's thin LTO re-converges at the final link
  so the looser per-package codegen doesn't hurt runtime).
- `justfile check-no-pyo3-in-cores`: extended to enumerate the new crate
  (the gate script uses shell-word-split, so the workspace-list addition
  is the workflow-mandated step).

### Sub-step C — companion routing + §4.3 oracle-retirement
**Routing cutovers:**
- `aerodrome/functions.py::calc_exact_in_stable`: now routes through
  `degenbot_rs.solidly_calc_exact_in_stable_solidly` (Solidly/Aerodrome
  pre-baked entrypoint). The Python `Fraction` fee is split into
  `fee.numerator` + `fee.denominator` at the seam. Removed the now-
  unused `_k_aerodrome` / `_get_y_aerodrome` / `_calc_exact_in_stable`
  imports from `calculations.solidly_stable` — the wrapper is no longer a
  closure-binder; it's a routing shim.
- `aerodrome/v2_pool_calc.py::_calc_tokens_out_stable`: routes through
  the `solidly_calc_exact_in_stable_solidly` Rust seam (imported as
  `_rs_calc_exact_in_stable_solidly`).
- `aerodrome/v2_pool_calc.py::_calc_tokens_out_volatile`: routes through
  the `solidly_calc_exact_in_volatile` Rust seam (imported as
  `_rs_calc_exact_in_volatile`).
- `aerodrome/pools.py:484`'s `_stable_swap_fn` closure delegates via
  `aerodrome.functions.calc_exact_in_stable` — updated transparent,
  no separate change required (the closure picks up the routed wrapper
  by Python's normal import resolution).

**§4.3 oracle-retirement:**
No new value-equivalence test was added — exactly one live
implementation per swap-math concern remains. The orchestration-level
gate is `tests/aerodrome/test_aerodrome_solidly_math_routing.py` (3
tests):
- `TestFunctionsRouting::test_calc_exact_in_stable_routes_through_rust`:
  `_Spy` on the `solidly_calc_exact_in_stable_solidly` symbol imported
  into `aerodrome.functions`; asserts the seam was hit exactly once with
  the right 8 positional args (including the `(fee_numer=997,
  fee_denom=1000)` pair from the routed `Fraction(997, 1000)` Solidly
  0.3% fee).
- `TestPoolCalcRouting::test_stable_swap_routes_through_rust` /
  `test_volatile_swap_routes_through_rust`: `_Spy` on the strategy-layer
  imports; asserts the companion's `calculate_tokens_out_from_tokens_in`
  hits the appropriate Rust seam (and not the wrong one — a stable pool
  swap shouldn't touch the volatile seam and vice-versa).

This is the §4.5 delegation-detection the rubric recommends for routing
cutovers whose math already has a parity test — NOT a §4.3
value-equivalence tautology. The byte-for-byte parity lives at the unit
level in `degenbot-solidly-math/tests/oracle_crosscheck.rs` (frozen
snapshot, no live Python import in the test loop), and the on-chain
parity lives in the §4.4 golden-replay harness in
`test_aerodrome_v2_onchain_parity.py`.

### Sub-step D — parity cross-check (frozen snapshot)
**New:** `rust/crates/degenbot-solidly-math/tests/oracle_crosscheck.rs`
+ `rust/crates/degenbot-solidly-math/tests/oracle_snapshot.txt`.

The snapshot is a JSON corpus of 411 `(args, result)` pairs across the
nine ported functions (60 calc_d / 19 calc_k / 60 calc_f / 60
calc_exact_in_volatile / 60 get_y_solidly / 60 f_camelot / 19 k_camelot
/ 60 get_y_camelot / 20 calc_exact_in_stable_solidly / 23
calc_exact_in_stable_camelot), generated once with a fixed RNG seed on
the pre-routing tree. Every snapshot case is checked against the Rust
port with a byte-for-byte assertion. The snapshot serializes every
integer as a JSON decimal-string to avoid `serde_json`'s `f64` fallback
for >u64 precision values — the cross-check parses them via
`U256::from_str_radix(s, 10)`.

The snapshot is a frozen, version-checked artifact (mirrors the
`degenbot-curve-math` + `degenbot-balancer-math` snapshot conventions).
Re-running the Python to regenerate the corpus is a separate deliberate
step — if the Python oracle changes shape, the snapshot must be
regenerated; it's not silently auto-regenerated.

A 480-case end-to-end Python ↔ Rust parity battery was also run during
implementation (across the Solidly + Camelot orchestration paths,
multiple reserve/decimal/fee combinations) — all green. This was a
one-shot verification harness used during the red-green loop, NOT a
committed test (would be the §4.3 anti-pattern; the committed
oracle_crosscheck.rs is the stability-checked mirror).

### §4.3 selective retention (justified)
- The Python `calculations/{solidly_stable,camelot}.py` modules stay:
  they are the live parity-oracle corpus for
  `tests/test_calculations.py`'s unit-math identity tests (each test
  asserts the math itself: `calc_d(x, x) ≈ 3·x^3·x + x^3·x = 4·x^4`,
  `calc_exact_in_volatile(amount_in, 0, r0, r1, fee)` reduces to
  constant-product). These are NOT Rust-vs-Python equivalence tests —
  they're unit-math identity checks against hand-computed expected
  values; they retire only when a future Rust leaf is wired through the
  seam AND those tests' expected-value derivations route through the
  Rust leaf in test fixtures.
- `tests/aerodrome/test_aerodrome_v2_onchain_parity.py` stays: it
  validates the routed Rust path against the deployed Aerodrome
  contract's `getAmountOut` via golden-replay (record: Anvil fork of
  Base mainnet @ block 46,875,151; replay: offline). The routing
  cutover changes this test's meaning (it now validates Rust-vs-on-chain
  rather than Python-vs-on-chain) but NOT its role — it remains the
  §4.4 Anvil/on-chain parity that ground-truth checks the deployed-
  contract rounding behavior a unit fixture corpus can't reach.

## Per-acceptance check

- ✓ Pure-Rust core leaf: `degenbot-solidly-math` (alloy-only, no `pyo3`,
  no `tokio`). All 10 expected entrypoints ported.
- ✓ PyO3 bindings: 10 `#[pyfunction]`s registered in `c_api::register()`
  under the `solidly-math` cargo feature; `.pyi` stub signatures added.
- ✓ Umbrella re-export: `pub use degenbot_solidly_math;` in
  `rust/crates/degenbot/src/lib.rs`; standalone-consumer smoke
  (`standalone_consumer.rs` step 6) calls `solidly_calc_d` + `solidly_calc_f`
  and asserts the analytic identity — no `pyo3` in the build graph
  (`just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` green).
- ✓ Companion routing: `aerodrome/functions.py::calc_exact_in_stable` +
  `aerodrome/v2_pool_calc.py::{_calc_tokens_out_stable,
  _calc_tokens_out_volatile}` route through Rust seams (delegation-
  detection test green). `aerodrome/pools.py`'s `_stable_swap_fn`
  closure picks up the routed wrapper transparently.
- ✓ Parity cross-check green: `degenbot-solidly-math/tests/
  oracle_crosscheck.rs` (10 cross-checks, 411 snapshot cases), all
  green on a clean tree.
- ✓ §4.3 oracle-retirement: no new value-equivalence test added — the
  §4.5 delegation-detection harness is the orchestration-level proof the
  rubric recommends for routings whose math already has a parity test.
- ✓ Camelot variant dispositioned: `f_camelot` / `k_camelot` /
  `get_y_camelot` ported 1:1; the Python oracle stays as the parity
  corpus for `tests/uniswap/v2/test_liquidity_pool_camelot_fold.py` +
  `test_camelot_v2_onchain_parity.py` (those tests' roles unchanged by
  the cutover — they remain §4.4 on-chain parity + a fold-equivalence
  test that's about pool-state machinery, not k/y variant math).

## Validation Gates

- `just test-rust` — green (incl. `degenbot-solidly-math/tests/
  oracle_crosscheck.rs` 10 cross-checks).
- `just test-rust-python` — green (199 passed).
- `just test-python` — green (2911 passed, +3 routing tests vs. before
  the task).
- `just lint-rust` — green (`clippy --deny warnings`; 3 docstring
  `# Errors` sections added to the infallible wrapper functions whose
  return type is `PyResult<PyObject>` only for the inner
  result-`int` conversion).
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — green (solidly-math leaf is
  pyo3-free under default features).
- `just lint-python` — green (ruff + ty; the .pyi stub additions are
  typed).
- `just format` — green (no diff after the `calc_exact_in_stable`
  wrapper reshape).

## Result

Close as `done`. One commit rolled up (5dd4da68). Exactly one live
implementation per Solidly/Camelot swap-math concern remains — the Rust
leaf `degenbot-solidly-math`. The Python oracle is retained as the
parity corpus for the unit-math identity tests + the §4.4 on-chain
parity harness; the §4.3 anti-pattern (a duplicate Rust-vs-Python
equivalence test between two live implementations) is not present.

data.title: Investigate V3-V3-V4 cmd_executor intermediate-token settlement failures
data.body:
## Goal

Figure out why the V3-V3-V4 permutation run reverts with `ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance` at the INTERMEDIATE WBTC hop (hop[1]), and fix it.

## Context

The cmd_executor smart contract is designed to NEVER require custody of intermediate (non-profit) tokens — every intermediate token output by hop[N] must be routed directly to where hop[N+1]'s callback pulls from, via the command stream. The V3-V3-V4 path violates this for WBTC at hop[1].

Verified against the sim-diag (from the blocked T2 investigation):
- Path: V3 (WBTC/WETH, zfo=False) → V3 (intermediate) → V4 (terminal).
- hop[0] is V3 `zfo=False` on the WBTC/WETH pool: token0=WBTC, token1=WETH. `zfo=False` = WETH IN, WBTC OUT. The first input is WETH (flash-borrowed), which the executor always has.
- The "transfer amount exceeds balance" revert fires at hop[1] (the intermediate WBTC hop): the executor receives WBTC from hop[0], then must send it to the hop[1] V3 pool via the V3 swap callback. The revert means the executor's WBTC balance is 0 at that callback — hop[0]'s WBTC output did not route to where the hop[1] callback pulls from.
- This is a COMMAND-STREAM ENCODING / SETTLEMENT-ORDER issue, NOT a first-token funding gap.

## Scope of investigation

1. **Trace the V3-V3-V4 cmd-stream encoder** (`_3hop_v3_v4_v3` in `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` + the primitives in `examples/cmd_stream.py`). Identify the exact settlement-order / token-routing instruction that places hop[0]'s WBTC output somewhere the hop[1] V3 swap callback does NOT pull from.
2. **Compare against a working V3-V3-V3 path** (which settles correctly) to find the divergent instruction.
3. **Make a definitive ruling on T2 (JHVE32):** was the original "funding pre-check" premise truly invalid? If confirmed invalid (as the blocked note argues), DROP T2. If the investigation surfaces a genuine funding gap the pre-check would catch, re-scope T2 instead.
4. **Propose the minimal fix** to the encoder (the settlement-order / token-routing instruction) so the intermediate WBTC lands where hop[1]'s callback pulls from — matching the cmd_executor's no-custody design. Do NOT implement in this task; promote to a focused fix task.

## Logs / evidence

- `logs/perm-V2-V3-V4.log`, `logs/perm-V3-V3-V4.log` — the failing paths.
- `logs/perm-V2-V3-V3.log`, `logs/perm-V3-V3-V3.log` — working V3-terminated paths for comparison.

## Deliverable

A written finding (in this task body) with:
- The exact encoder instruction that's wrong (file:line).
- The divergence from the working V3-V3-V3 path.
- A definitive ruling on T2 (drop or re-scope).
- A one-paragraph fix proposal (promoted to a separate task — do NOT implement here).

## Finding — V3-V3-V4 cmd_executor settlement failure (path 3179, block 25398584)

### Failing path (grounded in sim-diag; engine_state == onchain_state for ALL hops — NO drift)

Token chain: WETH →(hop0 V3)→ WBTC →(hop1 V3)→ USDC →(hop2 V4)→ WETH

- hop0 V3 0x9b5699 (WBTC/WETH), zfo=False → WETH in, WBTC out. out_a=0xa5=165.
- hop1 V3 0xA9390e (WBTC/USDC), zfo=True → WBTC in, USDC out. out_b=0x18e24=102180.
- hop2 V4 0xb9fd8b8b (USDC/WETH), zfo=True → USDC in, WETH out. out_c=0x3b29ebeec8b3.

optimal_input=0x397fa4725590 (WETH, flash-borrowed). The executor custodies ONLY WETH by design — all intermediate tokens (WBTC, USDC) must route pool-to-pool, never through the executor's balance.

### Decoded cmd_stream (140 bytes, byte-identical regen from `_3hop_v3_v3_v4`)

SET_ADDRESS tbl0=V3a, tbl1=V3b, tbl2=USDC; BEGIN_EXECUTION; then:
1. `V4_SYNC` currency=tbl2(USDC) — top-level, outside unlock
2. `V3_SWAP_COMPACT` V3b zfo=1 amount=165(out_a) recipient=PM flen=57 [b_fwd:]
   3. `V3_SWAP_COMPACT` V3a zfo=0 amount=optimal_input recipient=V3b flen=40 [a_fwd:]
      4. `V4_UNLOCK` inner_len=38 [v4_inner:]
         5. `V4_SETTLE`
         6. `V4_SWAP_COMPACT` c0=USDC c1=WETH amount=101924(out_b) exact-input
         7. `V4_TAKE_COMPACT` currency=WETH recipient=V3a amount=optimal_input
         8. `V4_SETTLE_ALL`

### Root cause (strongest hypothesis; honest about uncertainty below)

`V4_SETTLE_ALL` (opcode 8, the LAST instruction — matching the deep gasUsed=262579) reconciles per-currency PM deltas to zero. On the USDC side:
- `V4_SETTLE` (opcode 5) credits the ACTUAL USDC deposited by V3b's optimistic transfer-to-PM (the onchain V3b output, call it X).
- `V4_SWAP_COMPACT(out_b=101924)` (opcode 6) debits a STATIC exact-input (the engine's computed `out_b`) from the USDC delta.

If `X < out_b` (the onchain V3b output is less than the engine's static `out_b`, e.g. because the solver's `int_simulate_v3_swap` — a U512 re-implementation, distinct from onchain V3 cl-math — rounds `out_b` higher than the EVM), the net USDC delta is negative → `V4_SETTLE_ALL` reconciles via `sync(USDC); IERC20(USDC).transfer(PM, out_b - X)` FROM the executor. The executor holds 0 USDC (no-custody design) → **`ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance`**.

`matches_solver: null` on hop1 in the sim-diag confirms `out_b` was NEVER verified against the onchain recompute (this log predates T1's engine recompute), so a rounding divergence went undetected.

### Fix direction (corroborated, not definitively proven)

Replace `V4_SWAP_COMPACT(out_b static)` + `V4_SETTLE_ALL` with **`V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC`** (consumes the ACTUAL deposited USDC via PM exttload, eliminating the residual delta). Evidence: `_3hop_v3_v4_v3` (V3-V4-V3) uses `V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC` and has **0** "transfer amount exceeds balance" reverts across the run; V3-V3-V4 uses `V4_SWAP_COMPACT(out_b)` and has **116**. This mirrors the V2-V2-V4 fix (commit 2e505536) which already switched to V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC + V4_TAKE_DELTA for the same reason ("avoid CurrencyNotSettled when V3a's on-chain deposit or the V4 swap's on-chain output differs from the solver's out_a/out_b").

Now that T1 (recompute) is landed, fresh runs will ALSO surface a `matches_solver: false` on hop1 if the engine's `out_b` genuinely diverges from onchain — confirming the rounding-divergence sub-hypothesis.

### Uncertainty (honest)

1. **Reproduction:** the bug is NOT reproducible on the fake PoolManager (the agent's fake-PM repro passes). It is mainnet-specific — consistent with the fake PM's V3 pools using the same math as the engine (so X == out_b there), while mainnet V3 rounds differently.
2. **out_b verification inconclusive:** the T1 bounded single-step recompute against hop1's onchain state returns `None` — the 165-WBTC swap crosses the tick-grid boundary (165/108415 ≈ 0.15%, large enough to cross at tick_spacing=10), so verifying `out_b` against onchain requires the FULL tick map (a heavy RPC fetch not done here). The rounding-divergence sub-hypothesis is therefore plausible but not yet confirmed.
3. **Perm correlation is imperfect:** V3-V4-V4 uses `V4_SWAP_COMPACT` ×2 and does NOT revert; V4-V4-V3 uses `V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC` and DOES (14). So `V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC` alone isn't a universal fix — the residual-delta-trigger depends on WHERE the static-amount V4 swap sits relative to a V3 deposit + whether `V4_SETTLE_ALL` runs. The clean contrast is V3-V3-V4 (static + settle_all + post-V3-deposit V4 swap → revert) vs V3-V4-V3 (dynamic → no revert).

### Definitive ruling on T2 (JHVE32) — DROP IT

T2 as written: "Add funding pre-check on the FIRST input token before sim." **Definitively invalid.** The first input is WETH (flash-borrowed, always available — verified: hop0 zfo=False on WBTC/WETH = WETH in). The investigation surfaced NO funding gap a first-token pre-check would catch: the failure is a V4 delta-settlement / static-amount encoder issue, not a custody/funding gap. A first-token pre-check is a no-op for this path. **T2 is dropped.** (A pre-check on INTERMEDIATE-token custody would also be a no-op here — the executor holding 0 USDC is BY DESIGN, not a gap to catch; the fix is to stop demanding the executor transfer it.)

### Promoted fix task

Created as a separate task (do NOT implement in this investigation): switch the V3-V3-V4 (and V3-V4-V2, V4-V4-V3) terminal/middle V4 swap from `V4_SWAP_COMPACT(static out_b)` to `V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC` (consume actual deposited amount), mirroring `_3hop_v3_v4_v3` + the V2-V2-V4 2e505536 precedent. Verify with fresh-run T1 `matches_solver` on hop1 post-fix.

data.title: Provider I/O + chainlink price oracle: degenbot-rpc routing review
data.body:
## Goal
- Confirm `provider/*` delegates to `degenbot-rpc` where the Rust core owns the RPC path; confirm `chainlink/price_feed.py` stays Python (price-oracle I/O).

## Context
- Rust: `degenbot-rpc` (sync+async Alloy provider, `Contract`, WS subscription double-buffer); binding wrappers in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/rpc/`. `PyBotIo` (slice 14) owns the sync RPC choreography for build/update.
- Python: `src/degenbot/provider/{sync_adapter,async_adapter,factory,protocols,subscription,log_fetching,block_helpers,call_helpers,offline_provider,alloy_errors}.py`. Async-builder RPCs were deferred in slice 14 — evaluate async `PyBotIo` (`port-now` vs `stays-python`).
- `chainlink/price_feed.py` — price oracle with subscription/refresh lifecycle → `stays-python` per the ADR-003 token-state split (Python owns the price oracle).

## Acceptance
- Sync provider path confirmed delegating (or routed) through `PyBotIo`/`degenbot-rpc`; async `PyBotIo` dispositioned; chainlink recorded `stays-python` w/ criterion. `provider/CONTEXT.md` updated if seams moved.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`; `just test-rust-python`; `just test-python`; `just lint-rust`; `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`; `just lint-python`; `just lint-context-maps`; `just format`

> Rubric §2 evaluation complete. No cutover required — sync path already
> delegates through `degenbot-rpc`; async `PyBotIo` dispositioned
> `stays-python`; chainlink confirmed `stays-python`.

## Disposition record

### 1. Sync provider path — `done`
`ProviderAdapter` (`sync_adapter.py`) wraps `AlloyProvider`
(`degenbot_rs.AlloyProvider` → `degenbot-rpc::PyProvider`) for every RPC
method (`get_block_number`, `call`, `get_logs`, `get_code`, `get_balance`).
The `SyncSubscriptionSupport`/`Subscription` route WS subscriptions through
`degenbot_rs.AlloySubscription` (`degenbot-rpc::Subscription`). `Bot.build_pool`
+ the sync update path drive all build/update RPC choreography through
`PyBotIo` (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/py_bot_io.rs`, slice 14),
which releases the GIL for each multi-RPC sequence. `factory.py` is the
URL→adapter construction seam (ADR-006 D5). The sync path is fully delegated;
no linger.

### 2. Async `PyBotIo` — `stays-python` (criterion recorded)
Slice 14 deferred porting `AsyncPyBotIo` to Rust. Re-evaluated under §2.1:
the rationale for the *sync* `PyBotIo` port was GIL release across a
sequential multi-call RPC sequence (§2.1 "GIL bottleneck? Yes"). The async
build path (`AsyncBot.build_pool` → `AsyncPoolBuilder` → `AsyncPoolIO` over
`AsyncProviderAdapter`) already yields the GIL on every `await` to
`AsyncAlloyProvider` (`degenbot-rpc`, `pyo3-async-runtimes`); there is no
held-GIL compute window for a Rust port to recover. **Criterion: no GIL
bottleneck in the async path (Python-ecosystem coupling of `async def`
builder dispatch + IO-protocol parameterization), and `AsyncProviderAdapter`
already delegates per-call RPC to async Rust.** `port-now` would duplicate
the builder-orchestration surface Python already owns (the
`AsyncPoolBuilder` and `PoolIO`/`AsyncPoolIO` protocol seam in
`builders/pool_io.py`) without a perf bridge — reverse of ADR-003's
"delete, not migrate."
Live async build flow: `async_bot.py:build_pool` → `_dispatch_build` →
`AsyncPoolBuilder.build(io: AsyncPoolIO)` (`builders/protocol.py`,
`builders/async_v3_pool_builder.py`).

### 3. `chainlink/price_feed.py` — `stays-python`
`ChainlinkPriceContract` — on-chain price oracle with `price`/`decimals`
fetch + refresh lifecycle. Per ADR-003 token-state split: Python owns the
price oracle (refresh/subscription lifecycle + `Fraction` display) — the
underlying `eth_call` already routes through `eth_abi`/`web3`/`checksum_cache`
(Rust-backed checksum). Criterion §2.1 "I/O shape: price-oracle refresh
lifecycle" + "Python-ecosystem coupling (`web3`, refresh orchestration)."

## CONTEXT.md

No seams moved. `provider/CONTEXT.md` already documents
`alloy_errors.py` as the deliberate Python-side FFI error-translation seam
(FSI parity over the flattened Rust `ProviderError`); the
`PyBotIo`/`AsyncPoolIO` topology is recorded in `bot.py` /
`builders/pool_io.py`. No update required.

## Validation Gates

Evaluation-only disposition sweep (no code change):

- `just test-python` — green (2942 passed).
- `just lint-python` — green (ruff + ty, no diff).
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` — green (sync path already routes through
  the cores; async `PyBotIo` is `stays-python`, so no new pyo3 work).

## Result

Fast close: sync path `done`, async `PyBotIo` `stays-python` (criterion: no
GIL bottleneck — async `await` releases the GIL, and per-call RPC is
already on async Rust), chainlink `stays-python` (ADR-003 price-oracle
split). Exactly one implementation per concern remains.

data.title: Golden on-chain parity — Ethereum remaining pools
Switch V4 terminal swaps to V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC to eliminate residual-delta reverts
data.body:
## Goal

Fix the V3-V3-V4 (and V3-V4-V2, V4-V4-V3) "ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance" reverts by replacing static-amount `V4_SWAP_COMPACT(out_b)` with `V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC` (consumes the actual deposited amount via PM exttload), eliminating the residual USDC delta that `V4_SETTLE_ALL` currently tries to reconcile via an executor→PM transfer of a no-custody intermediate token.

## Root cause (from QGV7ME investigation)

`V4_SETTLE_ALL` reconciles per-currency PM deltas to zero. On the USDC side:
- `V4_SETTLE` credits the ACTUAL USDC deposited by V3b's optimistic transfer-to-PM (onchain V3b output, X).
- `V4_SWAP_COMPACT(out_b_static)` debits the engine's computed `out_b` (101924) from the delta.

If `X < out_b` (solver's `int_simulate_v3_swap` U512 rounds higher than EVM V3 cl-math), the net USDC delta is negative → `V4_SETTLE_ALL` does `sync(USDC); IERC20(USDC).transfer(PM, out_b-X)` from the executor → executor holds 0 USDC (no-custody design) → `ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance`.

## Fix

Mirror `_3hop_v3_v4_v3` (V3-V4-V3, 0 reverts) + the V2-V2-V4 precedent (commit 2e505536):
- Replace `V4_SWAP_COMPACT(out_b)` + `V4_SETTLE_ALL` with `V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC` + `V4_TAKE_DELTA` (take the actual produced forward_b output → V3c/recipient), so the V4 swap consumes exactly what V3b deposited → zero residual.

## Files / encoders to fix

- `_3hop_v3_v3_v4` (examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py:2493) — 116 reverts.
- `_3hop_v3_v4_v2` (examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py) — 54 reverts.
- `_3hop_v4_v4_v3` (examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py) — 14 reverts (verify the same root cause; uses V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC already for ONE swap, but still reverts — check which swap is static).

## Verification (Red → Green TDD)

1. Write a test that reproduces the V3-V3-V4 revert on the fake PoolManager with a DIFFERENT-onchain V3 output (engine out_b > onchain deposit X) — currently the fake-PM repro passes because the fake V3 uses the same math as the engine. To reproduce: make the fake V3b output LESS than the static out_b baked into the V4 swap command.
2. Switch to V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC and confirm the test goes green (no residual delta → no executor transfer → no revert).
3. Fresh permutation run: confirm V3-V3-V4/V3-V4-V2/V4-V4-V3 have 0 "transfer amount exceeds balance" reverts, and that T1's `matches_solver` on hop1 now surfaces `true` (engine out_b == onchain, post-fix) OR `false` (rounding divergence — the dynamic swap absorbs it either way).

## Out of scope

- Investigating WHY `int_simulate_v3_swap` rounds differently than EVM V3 (if it does) is a SEPARATE task — the V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC fix is robust to rounding either way. Only pursue the rounding root cause if T1's `matches_solver` post-fix shows `false`.

## Depends on

QGV7ME (investigation, done), T1/XNWWA3 (recompute, done — needed for the matches_solver verification).

## Completion note (partial — 2 of 3 encoders fixed)

Fixed via commit 3589f60 (TDD: 2 RED-GREEN test files):
- _3hop_v3_v3_v4 (116 reverts): V4c swap COMPACT(out_b) → SWAP_DYNAMIC;
  WETH take → V3a TAKE_COMPACT(optimal_input) → TAKE_DELTA.
- _3hop_v3_v4_v2 (54 reverts): V4b swap COMPACT(out_a) → SWAP_DYNAMIC;
  WBTC take → V2c TAKE_COMPACT(out_b) → TAKE_DELTA.

Both mirror the V3-V4-V3 precedent + commit 2e505536 (V2-V2-V4) exactly:
SWAP_DYNAMIC consumes the actual settled PM delta (eliminating the residual
that triggered executor transfer of a no-custody intermediate token);
TAKE_DELTA takes the actual produced output; SETTLE_ALL sweeps dust.

3022 tests pass (+5 new), clippy clean, only pre-existing curve failures remain.

## V4-V4-V3 (14 reverts) — NOT fixed here, promoted as separate follow-up
V4-V4-V3 is a DIFFERENT root cause than V3-V3-V4/V3-V4-V2:
1. drift=True on hop[0] (V3-V3-V4 had NO drift — pure encoder bug).
2. Revert is Comp::_transferTokens (Compound COMP token contract), not
   vanilla ERC20.
3. Uses an executor-custody pattern (V4_TAKE forward_b→executor, then
   ERC20_TRANSFER forward_b→V3c, then V3c swap) — NOT the pool-to-pool
   no-custody pattern. The executor explicitly custodies the intermediate
   token here, which breaks the no-custody design.

The V4-V4-V3 fix requires a deeper restructuring: send forward_b DIRECTLY
to V3c via V4_TAKE (eliminating executor custody) + resolve the hop[0] drift.
Filed as a separate task.

data.title: Library resolver `resolve_rpc_uris`
data.body:
## Goal
- Add `degenbot.config.resolve_rpc_uris(chain_id, /, *, cli_http=None, cli_ws=None, fallback_http=None, fallback_ws=None) -> tuple[str, str]` implementing the standard RPC-URI cascade so any caller (library, the `degenbot` click CLI, the backrun example) shares one resolution path.
- Eliminates the per-call ad-hoc `http://localhost:8545` default that masks misconfiguration (the devcontainer crash the user hit).

## Context
- `src/degenbot/config.py` already holds `DegenbotConfig` (pydantic `BaseSettings`) with an `rpc: dict[ChainId, HttpUrl|WebsocketUrl|Path]` and `ws: dict[ChainId, WebsocketUrl]` + `CONFIG_FILE`/`load_config_from_file`. This task adds the resolver on top of that config-read primitive.
- ADR-006 (per-chain Bot orchestrator): RPC is keyed by chain id. The chain-id-discriminated envvar (`DEGENBOT_RPC_HTTP_CHAINID_{chain_id}`) makes the chain binding explicit and surfaces a missing/wrong chain as a clean error instead of a silent localhost fallback.
- Q4=B decision: the two URIs (http, ws) resolve **independently** — each walks its own cascade. http may come from CLI while ws comes from config.toml.
- Q3=B decision: no `localhost` default. If no source provides a URI, raise a typed error listing every source checked + how to set each.

## Resolution order (per URI, independently)
1. `cli_http` / `cli_ws` argument (explicit caller override, highest priority)
2. OS env `DEGENBOT_RPC_HTTP_CHAINID_{chain_id}` / `DEGENBOT_RPC_WS_CHAINID_{chain_id}` via `os.environ` (works with `export` in the devcontainer — NOT the .env-file dict)
3. `fallback_http` / `fallback_ws` (caller-supplied lower-priority candidates; used by the example to inject the deprecated `NODE_HOST_*` rebuilt URIs without leaking that naming into the library)
4. config.toml via `load_config_from_file(CONFIG_FILE)`: `rpc[chain_id]` / `ws[chain_id]`, rendered `str(HttpUrl)`/`str(WebsocketUrl)`
5. raise `RpcNotConfiguredError`

## Acceptance Criteria
- `resolve_rpc_uris(1, cli_http="https://x")` returns `("https://x", <ws from next layer>)` — CLI wins for http, ws falls through.
- `resolve_rpc_uris(1)` with `DEGENBOT_RPC_HTTP_CHAINID_1`/`DEGENBOT_RPC_WS_CHAINID_1` set in `os.environ` returns those URIs (use `monkeypatch.setenv` in tests; restore after).
- `resolve_rpc_uris(1)` with neither CLI, OS env, fallback, nor a populated config.toml `rpc[1]` raises `RpcNotConfiguredError` whose message names all four source layers and the exact envvar name for chain 1.
- `RpcNotConfiguredError` subclasses `ValueError` (so existing `pytest.raises(ValueError)` callers keep working) and lives in `degenbot.config`.
- Each URI resolves independently: providing only `cli_http` still raises (only for ws) when ws is unconfigured everywhere — i.e. the error is per-URI and the message says *which* of http/ws was missing.
- `fallback_http`/`fallback_ws` rank below OS env but above config.toml (verified by a test where OS env is unset, fallback is set, config has a value → fallback wins).
- No `localhost` literal anywhere in the resolver or its tests.
- Reading config.toml when `CONFIG_FILE` does not exist counts as "not configured" for that layer (no crash — `load_config_from_file` is only called when the file exists; otherwise skip to raise).

## Validation Gates
- `uv run pytest tests/test_config_rpc.py -p no:randomly` (new file, Red→Green)
- `uv run ruff check src/degenbot/config.py`
- `uv run mypy src/degenbot/config.py`

## Completion
- Added `resolve_rpc_uris(chain_id, /, *, cli_http, cli_ws, fallback_http, fallback_ws) -> tuple[str,str]` + `RpcNotConfiguredError(ValueError)` to `src/degenbot/config.py`.
- Cascade (per URI, independent): CLI arg > OS env `DEGENBOT_RPC_{HTTP,WS}_CHAINID_{cid}` > caller fallback > config.toml `rpc[cid]`/`ws[cid]` > raise. No localhost default.
- Implementation detail: `_resolve_one` returns `str|None`; `resolve_rpc_uris` raises explicitly so the error message names which of http/ws was missing (Q4=B independent).
- Known quirk surfaced: pydantic `str(HttpUrl)` normalizes empty path to trailing `/` (e.g. `http://h:8545/`). This matches the AC ("rendered str(HttpUrl)") and existing config.toml consumption behavior; tests assert the normalized form.
- NOTE for next task: the devcontainer ships a real `~/.config/degenbot/config.toml` with chain 1 = `http://host.containers.internal:8545`/`ws://…8546`. The example test suite must isolate CONFIG_FILE (tests use a tmp-path autouse fixture).
- Validation: 15 new tests pass; ruff + `ty check` clean; `tests/test_config_default_chain_id.py` still green.

data.title: Fix V4-V4-V3 executor-custody pattern + hop[0] drift (14 reverts)
data.body:
## Context

V4-V4-V3 reverts on mainnet with `Comp::_transferTokens: transfer amount exceeds balance` (14 reverts in `perm-V4-V4-V3.log`). NOT the same root cause as V3-V3-V4/V3-V4-V2 (already fixed in UISLED commit 3589f60). Three differences:

1. **drift=True on hop[0]** (V3-V3-V4 had NO drift — pure encoder bug). The V4a swap with static optimal_input + stale engine state produces wrong forward_a → V4b produces wrong forward_b → out_b wrong → revert.

2. **`Comp::_transferTokens`** — Compound's COMP token contract (0xc00e94Cb662C3520282E6f5717214004A7f26888), not vanilla ERC20. The executor tries to transfer COMP (forward_b) it doesn't hold.

3. **Executor-custody pattern** (not pool-to-pool). The current `_3hop_v4_v4_v3` encoder:
```
inner = enc_v4_swap_compact(ha, optimal_input)   # V4a: WETH → forward_a (STATIC optimal_input)
inner += enc_v4_swap_dynamic(hb)                  # V4b: forward_a → forward_b (DYNAMIC)
inner += enc_v4_take_compact(forward_b, executor, out_b)   # TAKE forward_b → executor (STATIC out_b)
inner += enc_v3_swap_compact(v3c, out_b, executor, forward_data=c_pay)  # V3c swap
inner += enc_v4_settle_all()
c_pay = enc_erc20_transfer(forward_b, v3c, out_b)   # executor → V3c (STATIC out_b)
```
The executor explicitly custodies forward_b (TAKE → executor, then ERC20_TRANSFER → V3c) — **breaks the no-custody design**. When actual forward_b (from V4b) < static out_b, the ERC20_TRANSFER(out_b) exceeds the executor's COMP balance → `Comp::_transferTokens: transfer amount exceeds balance`.

## Fix direction (investigate + implement)

1. **Send forward_b DIRECTLY to V3c** via V4_TAKE (eliminate executor custody): `enc_v4_take_delta(forward_b, v3c_idx)` — V3's optimistic transfer + the forward_data pays forward_b from V3c's balance, not the executor's. Remove the `c_pay = enc_erc20_transfer(...)` + rework the V3c swap.
2. **Resolve hop[0] drift** — investigate why the V4a pool has stale state (may be the V4 register-then-seed race from the earlier `f27d2f1a` finding, or the V4 verify desync). The encoder fix is robust to drift (DYNAMIC absorbs it), but the drift itself should be fixed.
3. **V4a swap uses static optimal_input** — this is the FIRST hop, executor has flash-borrowed optimal_input WETH, so static is fine here. No change needed.

## Depends on

UISLED (done), QGV7ME investigation (done).

## Completion note (encoder fix done; drift promoted as follow-up)

Done via commit d043227c (TDD: 3 RED-GREEN tests).

## What was fixed
V4-V4-V3 no longer custodies the intermediate token (forward_b=COMP). The old
encoder did V4_TAKE_COMPACT(forward_b, executor, out_b) then ERC20_TRANSFER
(forward_b, v3c, out_b) — routing COMP through the executor (which holds 0 of
it by design). When actual forward_b < static out_b, the ERC20_TRANSFER
exceeded the executor balance → Comp::_transferTokens revert (14 reverts).

Fix matches the executor own TestV4V4V3: V4_TAKE_COMPACT sends forward_b
DIRECTLY to V3c as the V3c swap forward_data. During V3c callback, the take
delivers forward_b to the V3c pool, satisfying V3 optimistic-input check.
c_pay ERC20_TRANSFER removed entirely. Executor never touches the intermediate.

3 new tests: forward_b direct to V3c (not executor), take is V3c forward_data,
no ERC20_TRANSFER of any token. 3025 passed (+3 new), only pre-existing curve.

## NOT fixed (promoted as separate task)
V4a hop[0] drift: sqrt_price/tick divergence (intermittent ~5e-4, 10-tick lag,
then recovers). Transient V4 state-sync lag (not the snapshot freeze). The
no-custody encoder uses static out_b, exact only when V4b actual output ==
out_b (no drift). When V4a drifts, actual forward_b != out_b → V3c static
swap fails (different error: V3 IIA, not Comp transfer). The drift fix is a
V4 pump/buffer/quiesce concern — separate task created.

data.body:
## Goal
- Route `abi_adapter.py` and `contract/decoding.py` through the `degenbot-abi` core (`AbiType`/`AbiValue`/decoder/encoder/signature_parser) + PyO3 wrappers in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/abi/`.

- Python: `src/degenbot/abi_adapter.py`, `src/degenbot/contract/decoding.py`, `src/degenbot/contract/addresses.py`.
- ABI types are intentionally string-interfaced at the Python boundary (per `rust/AGENTS.md` "ABI Types: String Interface Decision") — do NOT expose `AbiType` as a `#[pyclass]`.
- Likely `partial` — the Python adapter may wrap/cache things the Rust seam already provides.

## Acceptance
- Live encode/decode call sites route through `degenbot_rs.decode`/`encode`; parity cross-check (proptest roundtrip encode→decode — the standard ABI invariant) green; dead Python adapter code deleted; ABI string-interface contract preserved.

- `just test-rust`; `just test-rust-python`; `just test-python`; `just lint-rust`; `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`; `just lint-python`; `just format`

> chainlink price feed, Aerodrome functions, Aave extraction +
> liquidation_patterns) now route through the `degenbot-abi` core via the
> `degenbot.abi_adapter` seam. The `eth_abi` backend survives as the

functions in `abi_adapter.py` are the canonical Python ABI surface.

(`abi_decode` import). The ABI string-interface contract is preserved:
type strings in/out; `AbiType` is **not** a `#[pyclass]` (per
`rust/AGENTS.md`).

### 2. `contract/decoding.py` — `done` (closed under UY4FB5)

(checksummed).

### 3. Lingering direct `eth_abi.abi.*` callsites — `partial` → actioned
Pre-task: 24 callsites issuing raw `eth_abi.abi.{decode,encode}`
instead of routing through the seam. All decoded types are standard
(uint/int/address/bool/bytes/string) — fully covered by the Rust
`degenbot-abi` leaf; no fixed-point needed at these sites. Routed:

- `builders/v3_builder_base.py` — 6 decodes (factory/token0/token1 from
  `address`; `fee` `uint24`; `tick_spacing` `int24`; V3 slot0 7-tuple).
- `builders/v3_pool_builder.py` — 4 decodes (liquidity `uint128`;

  `uint128/int128`; final aggregate decode).

- `builders/v4_pool_builder.py` — 4 decodes (V4 liquidity /

- `chainlink/price_feed.py` — 2 decodes (`decimals` `uint8`; EAC feed

- `aave/extraction.py` — 6 decodes (Supply/Borrow/Repay/Withdraw/

The `AbiAdapter` class + module-level functions are alive (log_decoders

data.title: Emit recompute on drifted V3/V4 hops in sim-diag
data.body:
## Goal
- The `recompute` block in `[sim-diag]` JSON currently emits `null` for
  `expected_out_engine` / `expected_out_onchain` / `matches_solver` on
  exactly the hops that drift — i.e. the hops we most need attribution for.
  Emit a real recompute on drifted hops so we can distinguish "engine
  computed the right output for its stale state" from "engine math is wrong".

## Context
- sim-diag is emitted by `_emit_sim_diag` in
  `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` (~line 1657). Each hop carries
  `engine_state` + `onchain_state` + a `recompute` sub-object. Today the
  recompute is only populated when states match; drifted hops get `null`.
- The recompute should run the engine's own swap-math (V3/V4) against BOTH
  the engine's snapshotted state AND the onchain state, with the hop's
  `amount_in`, and report both expected outputs + whether the engine's
  reported `solver_out` matches the engine-state recompute.
- This is the keystone instrumentation: S1, T3, T5 all rely on it. Build it
  first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- For every V3/V4 hop in a reverted path's sim-diag, the `recompute` block
  is populated with: `expected_out_engine` (recompute against engine_state),
  `expected_out_onchain` (recompute against onchain_state),
  `matches_solver` (bool: expected_out_engine == hop.solver_out within
  tolerance).
- V2 hops already populate this correctly — leave them.
- Tolerance: 1 wei (rounding from sqrtPriceMath vs full PoolManager).
- A drifted hop where `matches_solver=true` proves the engine math is right
  given its (stale) state; the revert is pure drift. This is the
  discriminant S1 needs.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` — sim-diag emitter unit tests updated + green.
- Re-run one perm (V3-V4-V3) for 60s and confirm `[sim-diag]` lines now
  carry non-null `recompute` on drifted hops. Paste one in the task body.

## Completion note (final — onchain recompute added)
T1 is now COMPLETE. expected_out_onchain is populated for V3/V4 hops via a
bounded single-step compute_swap_step_v3 against the onchain scalar
slot0/liquidity. V3/V4 ticks are only initialized at multiples of
tick_spacing → liquidity is constant within one grid step → the single-step
is EXACT for non-crossing swaps (the thin-arb majority S1 identified;
amount_in/liquidity ≤ 1e-4) and returns None when the swap would cross the
grid boundary (genuinely needs the full onchain tick map — heavy RPC).

- recompute_cl_amount_out_onchain: bounded single-step, None on crossing.
- populate_v3v4_recompute_full: threads expected_out_onchain; matches_solver
  stays keyed off the engine recompute (drift discriminant), falls back to
  onchain only when engine recompute is absent.
- refresh_v3v4_recompute_onchain: post-fetch refresh (mirrors V2 refresh),
  wired into fetch_onchain.

Commits: 9ad36cfe (engine recompute) + 8d973462 (onchain recompute).
296 bot-crate tests, clippy clean, full workspace green.

web3-provider return types."

### 3. `utils/solady/libzip.py` — `delete` (actioned)

data.title: Implement pure-Rust `PathGraph` + iterative DFS
data.body:
Build the complete graph algorithm in the `degenbot-pathfinding` core leaf. This is sub-step A of the three-layer cutover (§3.1): pure-Rust core, zero pyo3, independently testable.

## Goal
- A fully functional, pure-Rust port of the Python pathfinding DFS that produces identical path sets
- The `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests serve as the first parity oracle; they mirror the in-memory fixture tests from `tests/pathfinding/test_permutation_filter_min_depth.py`

## Context
The Python module (`src/degenbot/pathfinding.py`) currently has these responsibilities that port to Rust:
1. **Graph construction** (`_prepare_graph`): build a multigraph (nodes = token IDs, edges = pools with `{pool_id, pool_kind}`). Python also does DB queries + dead-end pruning; the DB queries stay in Python (ORM), but the graph data structure + pruning move to Rust.
2. **Node valid depths** (`_compute_node_valid_depths`): precompute which depth positions each node can participate in, for lookahead pruning. Pure graph analysis.
3. **DFS** (`_dfs` / `_dfs_async`): recursive depth-first search from start token back to itself (cycles), with cycle detection, min/max depth bounds, `pool_type_per_depth` permutation filter, lookahead pruning, and `include_reverse` optimization. This is the hot path.

Key design decisions (resolved):
- **Pool type representation**: Python uses `type[LiquidityPoolTable | UniswapV4PoolTable]` (2 variants). Rust uses `pub enum PoolKind { V2V3, V4 }`. The mapping is 2-variant and stable. Python passes pool kinds as `u8` discriminants (0 = V2V3, 1 = V4).
- **Graph storage**: `HashMap<u64, Vec<Edge>>` adjacency list (not NetworkX dict-of-dict-of-dict). An `Edge` is `{ pool_id: u64, pool_kind: PoolKind }`. Multi-edges (parallel pools between the same token pair) are naturally supported by `Vec<Edge>`.
- **Cycle detection**: Python does `not in working_path` (linear scan, O(depth) per edge — quadratic in path length). Rust uses a `HashSet<(u64, PoolKind)>` visited set for O(1) membership test. This is a correctness-preserving optimization: the set of (pool_id, pool_kind) pairs on the current path is identical to the Python `working_path` list's contents.
- **DFS iteration**: iterative (explicit stack), not recursive. Avoids Python function-call overhead and recursion limits. The visit order must match the Python recursive DFS exactly (process neighbors in insertion order, yield complete paths, backtrack one step). The Python code iterates `graph[start_token_id].items()` — NetworkX preserves insertion order for adjacency dicts. Rust must preserve edge insertion order in the adjacency list `Vec`.
- **`include_reverse`**: when a path is yielded, also yield its reverse (`path_steps[::-1]`). Port this to Rust — it's a trivial in-place reversal before yielding.
- **`pool_type_per_depth`**: a `Vec<Option<Vec<PoolKind>>>` (length = exact hop depth). A `None` entry allows all pool kinds at that depth. Edges whose `pool_kind` is not in the allowed set are pruned before recursion. The filter implicitly caps `effective_max_depth` at its length.
- **`node_valid_depths`**: `HashMap<u64, Vec<bool>>` (or `HashSet<u64>` per node of valid depth indices). The lookahead prunse: before recursing into a neighbor, if the neighbor can't participate at the next depth, skip without recursing.

What stays in Python (I/O + orchestration):
- DB queries (SQLAlchemy) to fetch pools, tokens, addresses
- Traversal plan computation (`_prepare_traversal_plan` — Cartesian product of start/end tokens, FORWARD_AND_REVERSE optimization)
- Address resolution (map pool_id → ChecksumAddress / (manager_address, pool_hash))
- Token ID resolution (start_token → token_id lookup)
- `PathStep` dataclass construction

## API (Rust core)
```rust
/// Discriminant for the two pool-table families.
/// 0 = LiquidityPoolTable (V2/V3), 1 = UniswapV4PoolTable.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum PoolKind { V2V3, V4 }

/// A pool edge in the graph: which pool connects two tokens.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct Edge { pub pool_id: u64, pub pool_kind: PoolKind }

/// A multigraph: token IDs are nodes, pools are edges.
pub struct PathGraph { /* adjacency list: HashMap<u64, Vec<Edge>> */ }

impl PathGraph {
    /// Build from a flat list of (token0_id, token1_id, pool_id, pool_kind) edges.
    /// Edges are added in order; neighbor iteration preserves this order.
    pub fn from_edges(edges: Vec<(u64, u64, u64, PoolKind)>) -> Self;

    /// Remove nodes with degree <= 1, repeating until no such nodes remain.
    pub fn prune_dead_ends(&mut self);

    /// Precompute valid depth positions per node, for lookahead pruning.
    /// Returns Some(map) only when pool_type_per_depth is provided.
    pub fn compute_node_valid_depths(
        &self,
        pool_type_per_depth: &[Option<Vec<PoolKind>>],
    ) -> Vec<(u64, Vec<bool>)>;

    /// Depth-first search for all valid paths from start back to end (cycles).
    /// Yields paths as Vec<(pool_id, PoolKind)> in the same order the Python DFS would.
    pub fn find_paths(
        &self,
        start: u64,
        end: u64,
        min_depth: usize,
        max_depth: Option<usize>,
        include_reverse: bool,
        pool_type_per_depth: Option<&[Option<Vec<PoolKind>>]>,
        node_valid_depths: Option<&HashMap<u64, Vec<bool>>>,
    ) -> Vec<Vec<(u64, PoolKind)>>;
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PoolKind`, `Edge`, `PathGraph` types defined in `graph.rs` with the API above
- `from_edges` builds a correct adjacency-list multigraph (parallel edges preserved, insertion order preserved)
- `prune_dead_ends` removes degree-0 and degree-1 nodes iteratively until fixpoint (matches Python's `while tokens_to_prune := ... graph.remove_nodes_from(...)`)
- `compute_node_valid_depths` produces identical results to the Python `_compute_node_valid_depths` for the same graph + filter
- `find_paths` produces paths in the **same order** as the Python `_dfs` for all test fixtures (edge insertion order == neighbor visit order)
- `find_paths` honors `min_depth` (no path shorter), `max_depth` (no path longer), `include_reverse` (yields reversed path after each forward path), `pool_type_per_depth` (prunes by hop-type + caps max depth), and `node_valid_depths` (lookahead pruning)
- `pool_type_per_depth` with fewer entries than `max_depth` does not panic (the implicit cap)
- `#[cfg(test)]` module in `graph.rs` with unit tests mirroring the in-memory fixture from `test_permutation_filter_min_depth.py`:
  - The 4-pool V2 graph (WETH-A parallel edges + A-B + B-WETH)
  - 3-depth V2-V2-V2 filter yields only 3-hop paths (no 2-hop leak)
  - 2-depth V2-V3 filter caps max depth
  - `include_reverse` doubles output
  - `min_depth` / `max_depth` bounds
  - `prune_dead_ends` removes dead-end tokens
- All Rust unit tests pass: `cargo test -p degenbot-pathfinding`
- Clippy clean: `cargo clippy -p degenbot-pathfinding -- --deny warnings`

## Validation Gates
- `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p degenbot-pathfinding`
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p degenbot-pathfinding --all-targets -- --deny warnings`
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`

## Notes for the implementer
- The Python DFS is in `src/degenbot/pathfinding.py` (`_dfs` function). Read it carefully before implementing — every branch (cycle yield, max-depth return, pool-type filter, lookahead) must be reproduced.
- The iterative DFS must process neighbors in **insertion order** (the order edges were added via `from_edges`). This is critical for path-ordering parity.
- Use a `HashSet<(u64, PoolKind)>` for the visited-set (cycle detection). Push/pop on yielding.
- The `find_paths` return type is `Vec<Vec<...>>` (eager, not an iterator) because Python will consume it in one PyO3 round-trip. An iterator would cross the PyO3 boundary per-yield.

data.title: PyO3 wrapper: `find_paths_rust` function
data.body:
Sub-step B of the three-layer cutover (§3.2): thin PyO3 translator over the core leaf.

## Goal
- Expose `PathGraph::find_paths` to Python via a single `#[pyfunction]` round-trip
- Register the symbol in the Python module so `pathfinding.py` can import it

## Context
- Binding layer lives in `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/` (the `degenbot_rs` cdylib)
- Per-domain subdirs mirror the cores; create `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/pathfinding/mod.rs`
- The wrapper is a thin translator: extract Python args (flat lists of ints) → build `PathGraph` → call `find_paths` → wrap result as nested Python lists
- No business logic in the wrapper (Rule 3)
- The graph construction (`from_edges` + `prune_dead_ends` + `compute_node_valid_depths` + `find_paths`) all happen in one `py.detach()` call — the entire search is GIL-released

## API (PyO3 wrapper)
```python
# Exposed as degenbot_rs._pathfinding.find_paths_rust (or similar)
def find_paths_rust(
    edges: list[tuple[int, int, int, int]],  # (token0_id, token1_id, pool_id, pool_kind_u8)
    start_token_id: int,
    end_token_id: int,
    min_depth: int,
    max_depth: int | None,
    include_reverse: bool,
    pool_type_per_depth: list[set[int] | None] | None,  # None = no filter
) -> list[list[tuple[int, int]]]  # (pool_id, pool_kind_u8) per hop
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/pathfinding/mod.rs` exists with the `#[pyfunction] find_paths_rust` wrapper
- `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/lib.rs`: `#[cfg(feature = "pathfinding")] pub mod pathfinding;` added
- `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/c_api.rs`: `#[cfg(feature = "pathfinding")]` block registering `find_paths_rust` via `wrap_pyfunction!`
- The wrapper:
  - Extracts `edges` as `Vec<(u64, u64, u64, u8)>` from the Python list

data.title: Route Python companion through Rust + eliminate N+1 queries
data.body:
Sub-step C of the three-layer cutover (§3.3): route `pathfinding.py` through the Rust seam, eliminate the N+1 address-resolution queries, and delete the dead Python DFS.

## Goal
- `find_paths` and `find_paths_async` produce identical results to the current implementation, but backed by Rust
- The per-path-per-pool SQLAlchemy address queries (the main bottleneck) are eliminated by bulk-preloading addresses into a lookup dict during graph construction
- NetworkX dependency removed from the codebase (only used in this module)

## Context
- The existing tests in `tests/pathfinding/` are the parity oracle (§4.2): they test the public `find_paths`/`find_paths_async` API. If the Rust-backed implementation passes them, parity is proven.
- The current `_prepare_graph` already queries all pools (token0_id, token1_id, pool_id) from the DB. Extend these same queries to also select `address` (V2/V3) or `manager.address, pool_hash` (V4), building `dict[int, ChecksumAddress]` and `dict[int, tuple[ChecksumAddress, str]]` lookup tables during graph construction — zero additional DB round-trips.
- The traversal plan (`_prepare_traversal_plan`) and token-ID resolution stay in Python (they're DB/ORM concerns).
- `PathStep` dataclass stays; it's the Python-facing result type.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `src/degenbot/pathfinding.py` rewritten:
  - `_prepare_graph` still queries pools from the DB, but now returns BOTH the flat edge list (`list[tuple[TokenId, TokenId, PoolId, int]]`) for Rust AND the address lookup dicts (`dict[PoolId, ChecksumAddress]` for V2/V3, `dict[PoolId, tuple[ChecksumAddress, str]]` for V4)
  - `_compute_node_valid_depths`, `_dfs`, `_dfs_async` are **deleted** (the Rust core handles these)
  - `find_paths` and `find_paths_async` build the traversal plan in Python (unchanged), then for each (start, end, direction) triple call `find_paths_rust(...)` (the PyO3 function) with the flat edge list + search options, then map the returned `(pool_id, kind_u8)` pairs to `PathStep` objects using the preloaded address lookup dicts
  - `PathStep` construction: for `V2V3` pools, `address = v2v3_address_lookup[pool_id]`; for `V4` pools, `address, hash = v4_address_lookup[pool_id]`
  - The public signatures of `find_paths` and `find_paths_async` are **unchanged** (same args, same return type `Iterator[Sequence[PathStep]]` / `AsyncIterator[Sequence[PathStep]]`)
  - `find_paths_async` can delegate to the sync Rust call (the search itself is fast + GIL-released; the async wrapper just yields results as an async iterator). No need for an async Rust path.
- `networkx` removed from `pyproject.toml` `[project.dependencies]`
- `uv lock` succeeds and no longer includes `networkx`
- `import networkx` appears nowhere in `src/degenbot/`
- All existing pathfinding tests pass unchanged:
  - `tests/pathfinding/test_pathfinding.py`
  - `tests/pathfinding/test_permutation_filter_min_depth.py`
  - `tests/pathfinding/test_pool_type_per_depth.py`
- `ruff check src/degenbot/pathfinding.py` and `ruff format --check src/degenbot/pathfinding.py` pass
- `ty check src/degenbot/pathfinding.py` passes

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (full suite — confirms no regressions)
- `uv run pytest tests/pathfinding -x -q --no-header` (slow tests included)
- `uv run pytest tests/pathfinding/test_permutation_filter_min_depth.py -x -q --no-header` (the deterministic in-memory fixture — fast, proves exact parity)
- `uv run ruff check --fix src/degenbot/pathfinding.py`
- `uv run ruff format --check src/`
- `uv run ty check --no-progress src/`

## Notes for the implementer
- The edge list passed to Rust must be in the same order the Python `_prepare_graph` added edges to the NetworkX graph: iterate `pool_types` in order, and within each pool type iterate the query result in DB order. This ordering is critical for path-output parity (DFS visit order depends on neighbor insertion order).
- The `pool_type_per_depth` Python arg uses `set[type]` (Python class objects). Convert to `list[set[int] | None]` by mapping each pool-type class to its `PoolKind` discriminant: `issubclass(t, LiquidityPoolTable) → 0`, `issubclass(t, UniswapV4PoolTable) → 1`.
- For `find_paths_async`: since the Rust call is sync and GIL-released, the async generator can just call it synchronously and yield results. The `asyncio.sleep(0)` calls in the old `_dfs_async` are no longer needed (they existed to yield control between recursion levels; the Rust call is a single blocking operation).
- The `Direction.FORWARD_AND_REVERSE` → `include_reverse` mapping stays: set `include_reverse=True` when direction is `FORWARD_AND_REVERSE`.
- Do NOT remove `networkx` from `pyproject.toml` until ALL tests pass with the Rust-backed implementation. Remove it as the final sub-step.

data.body:
## Goal
- Rename the V2 constant-product pool class `LiquidityPool` → `UniswapV2Pool` so the V2 companion carries the same DEX+version identity naming as its `UniswapV3Pool` / `UniswapV4Pool` siblings.

## Context
During the ADR-005 three-layer migration, the V2 pool was rewritten as a Python companion over a Rust-owned `PyLiquidityPool` handle (`_from_py_pool` is the only construction seam; `__init__` raises). That rewrite erased the class's V2-identifying naming: it kept the legacy generic name `LiquidityPool` while V3 and V4 companions were introduced with proper `UniswapV3Pool` / `UniswapV4Pool` names (in `v3_liquidity_pool.py` / `v4_liquidity_pool.py`). This task restores the V2 identity. See `src/degenbot/uniswap/liquidity_pool.py:41` for the class def and `CONTEXT-MAP.md` "Uniswap" + "Rust Extension" module bullets for the companion/identity architecture.

## Decisions (resolved via repo convention — override if needed)
- **Hard rename, no backwards-compat alias.** Per AGENTS.md ("no backwards compatibility layer unless directed otherwise"), do NOT leave `LiquidityPool = UniswapV2Pool` as a deprecated re-export. Update all import sites.
- **File renamed too.** Symmetry with V3/V4 file layout is the point of restoring identity; keeping `liquidity_pool.py` would leave the inconsistency.
- **`LiquidityPoolError` stays.** It is a generic pool exception shared across V2/V3/V4 calc paths (`exceptions/pool.py:95`, raised from `v2_pool_calc.py`, `v3_pool_calc.py`, `v4_liquidity_pool.py`). Out of scope.
- **`LiquidityPoolTable`, `AbstractLiquidityPool`, `PyLiquidityPool` stay.** Substring collisions only; these are unrelated symbols (DB model, abstract base, Rust handle).

data.title: V3: stored tick fetcher + bitmap empty-word fix (Rust I/O)
data.body:
## Goal
- Promote the V3/V4 tick fetcher from per-call construction to a stored `Option<Arc<dyn TickWordFetcher>>` on `V3PoolState` (and `V4PoolState`, which shares the CL state shape), set at `register_v3_pool`/`register_v4_pool`. Delete the per-call `PyTickWordFetcher` construction in `PyLiquidityPool::calculate_tokens_out_with_fetch`.
- Make the Rust tick-bitmap representation faithful: a word the fetcher reported as checked-but-empty (`tickBitmap(word) == 0`) must survive in the derived bitmap so the sparse-fetch loop does not re-fetch forever, eliminating the companion-side `_bitmap_override` cache.

## Context
- The stored-trait-object pattern is *proven*: `TickWordFetcher` (pyo3-free, `rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/tick_fetch.rs:57`, `Send + Sync`) + `PyTickWordFetcher` (`rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/bot/pool.rs:40`, holds `Py<PyAny>`, GIL-safe) compile and run today — they are currently constructed per-call at `pool.rs:141/241/283/334`. This task *promotes* the adapter to constructed-once-at-registration + stored.
- Field on state: `V3PoolState`/`V4PoolState` gain `pub fetcher: Option<Arc<dyn TickWordFetcher>>`. `register_v3/v4_pool` gains an optional `fetcher: Option<Arc<dyn TickWordFetcher>>` param-threaded from `PyBot.register_v3_pool` (PyO3 accepts a Python callable, wraps it once via `PyTickWordFetcher`, stores the `Arc<dyn>`).
- Bitmap gap (companion comment at `v3_liquidity_pool.py:210`): "Rust derives the bitmap from `tick_data` KEYS only, so a word with no initialized ticks vanishes." Fix in `tick_fetch.rs`/the bitmap derivation: track checked-but-empty words (`HashSet<i32>` of known-empty words on the CL state, populated when a fetch returns an empty `FetchedTickWord`) so they appear present-but-zero in the derived bitmap.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `V3PoolState`/`V4PoolState` carry `fetcher: Option<Arc<dyn TickWordFetcher>>`; `register_v3/v4_pool` accept and store it.
- `calculate_tokens_out_with_fetch` reads the stored fetcher (no per-call `PyTickWordFetcher::new`). The call-time `fetcher` argument is *dropped* (registration is the single source); exception only if a test genuinely needs a per-call override, in which case keep it as `Option` and document why.
- A Rust unit test: register a pool with a fetcher that returns an empty word; assert a second solve does NOT re-invoke the fetcher (the empty word survived).
- No behavioral regression in V3/V4 sparse-map sims.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` — green, including the new no-re-fetch test.
- `just test-rust-python` — green (V3/V4 on-chain parity goldens unchanged).

## Note
- This task is the Rust I/O foundation for BOTH the V3 and V4 seams. V4's seam task depends on it. The bitmap fix is load-bearing for deleting `_bitmap_override` on both companions.

## Goal
- Define a pyo3-free `BalancerRateProvider` trait in `degenbot-bot` (method surface from the single call site: `self._rate_provider.get_rates` → `fn get_rates(&self) -> Result<Vec<U256>, _>` — audit `src/degenbot/balancer/stable_pools.py` for the full surface).

## Context
- Rate providers are **off-chain yield-bearing token price feeds** — NOT event-log-decodable — so the stored-trait-object is the *terminal* design (not debt): you cannot decode a rate from a Mint/Burn/Swap log. This is the Polars-codec pattern: core holds a pyo3-free trait, the binding supplies the Py adapter, a pure-Rust consumer supplies a pure-Rust `impl`.
- Call site: `src/degenbot/balancer/stable_pools.py:393` `rates = self._rate_provider.get_rates`. The `_StaticRateProvider` fallback (construction-time rates wrapped) becomes a pure-Rust `impl BalancerRateProvider` for `StaticRateProvider` — no Python.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `BalancerRateProvider` trait in pyo3-free core; `PyBalancerRateProvider` adapter compiles; stored on `BalancerStablePoolState`.
- A Rust unit test: static-rate provider returns construction-time rates; dynamic provider delegates to the Py callable.

data.title: Docs: ADR-005/006 status + migration guide
data.body:
## Goal
- Update ADR-005 identity/state-split footer + ADR-006 D4 status to record: all six non-V2 companions migrated to the sealed `_from_py_pool` seam; identity fully handle-readable; I/O callables (tick fetcher, Curve data_provider, Balancer rate_provider) are stored pyo3-free trait objects on `VxPoolState` (Py adapters in `degenbot-python`).
- Add a migration guide `docs/migration-guides/sealed-pool-seam.md` (the rubric: forbid `__init__`, `self = cls.__new__`, variant-family guard, identity off handle, single commit per family).
- Record the **layer-3 follow-up epic** (not built here): pump-decode Curve/Balancer event-decodable per-block state directly into `BotState` slots (eliminates the data_provider/rate_provider callables for on-chain feeds; Balancer off-chain rate feeds remain trait objects terminally).

## Context
- Mirrors the existing `docs/migration-guides/three-layer-transition.md` + the ADR-005 footer pattern.
- The follow-up epic note ensures the trait-object design isn't mistaken for terminal for on-chain Curve feeds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- ADR-005 footer updated; ADR-006 D4 status updated.
- Migration guide file exists with the rubric.
- Follow-up epic is recorded as a TODO in the migration guide.

## Validation Gates
- `just lint` — green (mdformat).

## Depends on
- All family seam tasks complete.

## Result
- commit pending
- `BotState::pool_family(pool_id) -> &'static str` added to `bot_core/mod.rs` — dispatches on `PoolEntry` variant directly.
- `PyLiquidityPool.pool_family` `#[getter]` in `degenbot-python/src/bot/pool.rs` delegates to it.
- `.pyi` stub synced (`pool_family` property).
- V2 `_from_py_pool` family guard migrated from `if not py_pool.variant` to `if py_pool.pool_family != "v2"`; renamed the Red test from `..._with_variant_error` to `..._with_family_error`.
- TDD: tracer-bullet test (V2 + unknown) → minimal dispatch Green → extended test covering all 6 families.

## Result
- commit a7ee423b
- Stored `Option<Arc<dyn TickWordFetcher>>` on V3PoolState/V4PoolState; `TickWordFetcher` trait gained `Debug` bound.
- `RegisterV3/V4PoolParams` gained `fetcher` field; `register_v3/v4_pool` (PyBot) accept `tick_data_fetcher` Python callable, wrap via `make_tick_fetcher`.
- 4 BotState fetcher methods (`calculate_tokens_out_with_fetch`, `simulate_exact_input/output_swap_with_fetch`, `simulate_swap_with_override`) dropped generic `<F>` + per-call arg; clone stored Arc.
- 5 PyLiquidityPool methods dropped `fetcher` parameter.
- `.pyi` stub synced.
- V3/V4 builders pass `tick_data_fetcher` at registration; companions drop `fetcher=` kwargs; test helpers + parity tests updated.
- Bitmap empty-word fix was already in place; new no-re-fetch test pins it.
